goldens.comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:71 — readInteger passes readLength()'s indefinite-length sentinel (-1) straight to read(length), causing `new byte[-1]` to throw an uncaught NegativeArraySizeException instead of a clean IOException
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: the code uses the indefinite-length sentinel value (-1) returned by readLength() as if it were a valid non-negative length. The golden comment highlights unexpected behavior when doing arithmetic with -1, while the candidate highlights another concrete failure mode (passing -1 to read() leading to a negative array size). In both cases, the root issue is unhandled indefinite-length encoding causing incorrect/erroneous processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:64 — detectProvider silently picks the highest-order provider instead of throwing IllegalStateException when multiple providers are found, an observable behavioral change for deployments relying on the old strict check, with no migration note or changelog reference

adjudication.rationale: The diff in common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java changes detectProvider from throwing IllegalStateException when foundProviders.size() > 1 to instead sorting providers by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and returning the first, only logging the rest at debug level. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change that could affect deployments that previously failed fast on multiple providers. However, whether there is/was a migration note or changelog reference cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/AuthzClient.java — Behavioral change where AuthzClient.create() now invokes CryptoIntegration.init() has no accompanying test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a behavioral side-effect in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` by calling `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader());` before constructing the client. The only new test added (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) exercises ECDSA signature conversion via `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, but nothing in the diff tests that `AuthzClient.create()` triggers crypto integration initialization or that it selects/loads the expected `CryptoProvider` via the service loader. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly introduced nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java — No test covers detectProvider behavior with multiple providers on the classpath or order()-based tie-breaking, despite this being changed/introduced logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java` to sort discovered `CryptoProvider`s by the new `order()` (descending) and to no longer throw when multiple providers are present (it now picks the first and logs the rest). The PR adds only an ECDSA conversion test in `authz/client` and does not add any test exercising `detectProvider` behavior with multiple providers or order-based selection/tie-breaking. The finding’s file path is off (it’s under `common/...`, not `authz/client/...`), but the underlying missing-test concern is grounded in the diff.
